title: Data Science after a BA Economics

value.body: Economics already teaches statistics, econometrics and reasoning with data, which overlap with data science. Moving across usually means adding programming (Python or R, and SQL), machine-learning basics and project experience — through a master's degree or through certificates and self-study.

items.label: Master’s routes
items.value: M.Sc / MA in data science, statistics or economics with a quantitative focus

items.label: Typical first roles
items.value: Data analyst, business analyst, research analyst

value.title: How you get in
value.body: For a master's: a bachelor's degree, often with mathematics or statistics at some level, and admission through CUET-PG, a university or institute entrance test, or merit. Statistics-heavy programmes test mathematics closely. Certificates and online courses have no entrance — your own projects show your skill.

value.title: At a glance
items: A master's takes two years and costs more but gives structured training and campus hiring; certificates cost less but rely on a self-built portfolio.
Entry roles are more often data analyst or business analyst than data scientist.
Economics knowledge is useful in analytics for policy, finance, market research and consulting.
Gaps in linear algebra, calculus and probability are the usual hurdle.
